architecture_summary.operational_context: Hybrid on-premises and cloud identity infrastructure with Active Directory, Certificate Services, and Azure AD Connect synchronization.

threat_actors.name: External Opportunistic Attacker
threat_actors.motivation: Financial gain through credential theft and ransomware deployment
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Phishing or exploitation of exposed web enrollment services
non_capabilities: No physical access to on-premises data centers
No pre-existing insider knowledge of internal network topology
Cannot bypass MFA without valid credentials

threat_actors.name: Targeted Nation-State Actor
threat_actors.motivation: Espionage and long-term persistence in critical infrastructure
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Supply chain compromise or advanced persistent threat (APT) techniques targeting hybrid identity bridges
non_capabilities: Cannot physically access air-gapped root CA hardware
No direct access to offline backup tapes
Cannot compromise quantum-resistant encryption if implemented

threat_actors.name: Insider Threat - Malicious Admin
threat_actors.motivation: Sabotage or data exfiltration for personal or external gain
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Legitimate administrative access to Domain Controllers and PAM Vault
non_capabilities: Cannot bypass hardware security modules (HSMs) protecting root CA keys
No access to cloud-only resources not synced to on-prem
Cannot delete audit logs from immutable SIEM storage

attack_paths.technique_name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket
attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised Domain Controller or NTDS.dit exfiltration
attack_paths.impact: Full domain compromise, ability to impersonate any user or service
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: krbtgt hash is a high-value target; if DC is compromised, golden ticket creation is trivial.

attack_paths.technique_name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
attack_paths.impact: Offline cracking of service account passwords, leading to lateral movement
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires valid domain user; common in environments with weak service account passwords.

attack_paths.technique_name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Silver Ticket
attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised ADCS server or certificate template abuse
attack_paths.impact: Forged certificates for authentication, bypassing MFA and conditional access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: ADCS misconfigurations (e.g., ESC1, ESC8) are prevalent and allow certificate-based authentication bypass.

attack_paths.entry_point: Web Enrollment Service exposed to internet
attack_paths.impact: Remote code execution or data exfiltration from ADCS
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Web services are common attack vectors; depends on patching and WAF configuration.

attack_paths.impact: Access to internal network and Domain Controllers
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Credential stuffing and phishing are common; VPN is a primary entry point for remote users.

attack_paths.impact: Lateral movement to Domain Controllers and PAM Vault
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Admin workstations are high-value targets; RDP is a common lateral movement vector.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised SCIM Provisioner or Azure AD Connect
attack_paths.impact: Creation of rogue cloud accounts or modification of sync rules for persistence
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Hybrid identity bridges are often overlooked; SCIM endpoints can be abused for account manipulation.

attack_paths.entry_point: Compromised MFA Gateway or Conditional Access Policy Engine
attack_paths.impact: Bypass MFA for all users, enabling persistent access
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: MFA Gateway is cloud-hosted and protected by Azure security controls; requires high-level compromise.

attack_paths.impact: Exfiltration of audit logs and sensitive identity data
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: SIEM connectors are typically monitored; exfiltration would be detected by anomaly detection.

attack_paths.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_paths.impact: Persistent access to endpoint, enabling further lateral movement
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Common persistence technique on endpoints; depends on endpoint detection and response (EDR) coverage.

mitigations.control_name: Access to local and remote assets is limited to authorized users, processes, and devices
The network is protected from threats internal and external to the organization
Audit logs are generated, stored, and protected
Access permissions and authorizations are managed using a least-privilege paradigm

findings.severity_rationale: Compromise of krbtgt hash allows full domain takeover, leading to complete loss of identity integrity.
Kerberoasting allows offline cracking of service account passwords, enabling lateral movement and privilege escalation.
ADCS misconfigurations allow certificate forgery, bypassing MFA and conditional access, leading to persistent access.
Exposed web enrollment services are vulnerable to exploitation, leading to remote code execution or data exfiltration.
Stolen VPN credentials provide direct access to internal network and Domain Controllers.
Compromised admin workstations enable lateral movement to critical systems, but require initial compromise.
SCIM provisioner compromise allows account manipulation for persistence, but requires high-level access.
MFA Gateway compromise is unlikely due to cloud security controls, but would allow MFA bypass.
SIEM connector compromise allows exfiltration of audit logs, but is likely to be detected.
Endpoint persistence allows continued access and lateral movement, but depends on EDR coverage.

agentic.blast_radius: Compromise of hybrid identity agents could lead to full domain and cloud identity compromise, affecting all users and services.
human_oversight_points: Regular review of SCIM sync logs
